name: Standing Lunge

load.note: Blue or yellow turns it into a balance-and-control version: the carriage is harder to hold steady.

summary: One foot on the floor beside the footbar, the other against the shoulder rest. The floor leg bends and the carriage leg slides back into a lunge.
steps: Stand beside the reformer near the footbar, inside foot on the floor next to the carriage.
Other foot on the carriage against the nearest shoulder rest; hands rest on the footbar.
Stand tall. Breathe out, bend the floor knee and let the carriage slide back.
Breathe in, straighten the floor leg to bring the carriage home.

layers.title: Pulses and holds
layers.text: Small pulses at the bottom, then hold.

layers.title: Hands free
layers.text: Let go of the footbar; add arm work.

layers.title: Front heel lifted
layers.text: Lift the front heel, or put a small ball under it.

layers.title: Raised
layers.text: Standing foot on a box or platform for more depth.

modifications: Lean the body slightly forward as the back leg goes out to ease the lower back.
Pregnancy and post-natal: use a lighter spring and keep the range small.

cautions.note: Reduce the depth; keep the shin vertical.
Keep both hands on the footbar.

cues:
Front knee stacks over the ankle and points over the middle toes.
Stay tall — ribs over hips.
Back knee stays off the carriage.
Control the return; no crashing home.

review.note: Draft entry written for OpenPilates. Needs review by a qualified Pilates instructor before teaching from it.
